To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

polyoma viral DNA sequences are stable during the growth of virus-transformed rat cells in vivo, that the pattern of virus-coded proteins is stable during tumor growth, and that the stability of the polyoma viral DNA and virus-coded proteins is not related to the growth rate of tumor cells.
polyoma virus DNA in transformed rat cell lines was stable during their in vivo passage and that polyoma virus-coded proteins were present in tumor cell lines after in vivo growth.
polyoma virus DNA and viral proteins are stably retained by transformed rat cells during tumor formation in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stability of the polyoma DNA sequences in the tumor cell genome and of the viral-coded proteins during tumor growth in vivo.
the stability of polyomas virus DNA sequences and virus-induced tumor antigens during the in vivo passage and growth of transformed cell lines.
the molecular basis of transformation by polyoma virus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the virus DNA is stable during the passage of the transformed cells.
polyoma virus DNA and polyoma virus tumor antigen expression is stable during tumor growth.
the polyoma DNA sequences, the polyoma virus tumor proteins, and the polyoma virus-induced cell transformation are all stable during in vivo growth of polyoma virus-transformed rat cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
polyoma virus tumor cells, after passage in vivo, are still characterized by the presence and stability of viral DNA sequences and virus tumor antigens.
the state and arrangement in transformed rat cells of polyoma virus sequences, and the pattern of polyomavirus tumor antigens in transformed rat cells, are stable after their growth in vivo.
the polyoma virus DNA is stable in the transformed cell line during its passage in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
polyoma viral DNA sequences and virus-encoded proteins are stably maintained in transformed cell lines after in vivo passage.
, during in vivo passage, there is a remarkable stability of the viral DNA sequences and the pattern of virus-coded proteins in the transformed cells.
the polyoma virus genome is remarkably stable in transformed cells and is not subject to major alterations during tumor formation.
